chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Verily, the nutfa (sperm-drop) remains in the womb for forty days, then it becomes a 'alaqa (clot) for forty days, then it becomes a mudgha (morsel of flesh) for forty days. When four months are complete, God dispatches two creative angels. They say: 'O Lord! What will You create — male or female?' So they are commanded. Then they say: 'O Lord! Wretched or happy?' So they are commanded. Then they say: 'O Lord! What is its appointed term, and what is its provision?' — and everything of its condition, and he enumerated several such things — and they write down the covenant between its two eyes. Then when God completes the appointed term for it, God sends an angel who rebukes it with a severe rebuke, and it comes out having forgotten the covenant.
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: I said to him: Is it permissible to supplicate God so that He changes a female to a male, and a male to a female? He said: God does whatever He wills.

key_terms.الرِّزْق: provision/sustenance — the divinely allotted share of worldly sustenance
key_terms.الْأَجَل: the appointed term — the divinely decreed lifespan of the individual
key_terms.الْمِيثَاق: the covenant/pact — the primordial agreement written between the infant's eyes at the time of formation
key_terms.شَقِيّ / سَعِيد: wretched/happy — eschatological categories determining whether a soul will be among the miserable or the blessed
key_terms.عَلَقَة: 'alaqa — the clot stage of embryological development, corresponding to Quranic usage (23:14)
key_terms.مَلَكَيْنِ خَلَّاقَيْنِ: two creative angels — angelic agents appointed to record the infant's destiny
key_terms.مُضْغَة: mudgha — the morsel of flesh stage, also referenced in the Quran (23:14)
key_terms.نُطْفَة: nutfa — the initial sperm-drop stage of embryological development

ai.seo_question: What does Al-Kafi say about the stages of embryonic development and the angels who record human destiny?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes the three stages of embryonic development — nutfa (sperm-drop), 'alaqa (clot), and mudgha (morsel) — each lasting forty days, and explains how, at four months, God sends two creative angels to record the child's sex, fortune, lifespan, and provision as a covenant inscribed between its eyes. At birth, an angel rebukes the soul, causing it to forget this primordial covenant. When al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asks whether du'a can change a child's sex, Imam al-Ridha (AS) affirms divine omnipotence: 'God does whatever He wills.' The hadith addresses the cosmological understanding of human origins, and the question of free will versus divine decree — matters of intense theological discussion in the early Shia community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said, 
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘The sperm happens to be in the womb for forty days, then it becomes a clot for forty days, then it becomes a lump for forty days. So when four months are complete, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sends two creating Angels, so they are both saying: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What will You<sup>azwj</sup> Created, male or female’. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Commands them both, and they are both saying: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Miserable or happy?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Commands them both, and they are saying: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is its term? And what is its sustenance?’, and everything from its state, and a number of things from that, and they both write these down as the covenant in between his eyes. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Completes the term for him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sends an Angel, so he rebukes him with a severe rebuke, and he forgets the Covenant’.

So Al-Hassan Bin Al-Jaham said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So is it allowed that he can supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Changes the female to a male, and the male to a female?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Sperm in the womb after forty days becomes a clot and after forty days thereafter it becomes an embryo. When four months are complete Allah sends two creating angels and they ask, “O Lord, what do You want to create? Do You want to create a male or a female.” They then receive the command. Thereafter they ask, “O Lord, do You want him to be virtuous or a wicked one?” They then receive the command. They ask, “O Lord, how much is the length of his life, how much is his sustenance, everything of his condition and the number of such things?” They write the covenant between his eyes. When the time of pregnancy is complete, Allah sends an angel who scolds him harshly. He comes out but has already forgotten the covenant.’

Al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm has said, that I then asked him (the Imam), ‘Will Allah because of prayer change female to a male and a male into a female?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah can do whatever He wants.’”
